patch:
@@ -3,8 +3,8 @@
 # exists so a stopped backup gets named").
 #
 # Read-only: it changes nothing and attempts no repair. It exits 0
-# only when BOTH hold, and otherwise exits 1 with one line per
-# violation naming the job/timer:
+# only when all applicable checks hold, and otherwise exits 1 with one
+# line per violation naming the job, timer, day, or archive:
 #   (a) pm-dashboard-backup's run record ($HOME/backups/dashboard/
 #       .last-run.json, written by modules/pm-dashboard-backup.sh on
 #       every exit path) says result=complete and finished within
@@ -22,6 +22,11 @@
 #       only an object listing sees the absence. Credentials come
 #       from Bitwarden exactly as in pm-dashboard-backup.sh, and
 #       rclone/bws resolve via PATH so tests can stub both.
+#   (d) when $HOME/backups/pm-stack exists, the newest valid day dir
+#       whose mtime is within the threshold contains its
+#       pm-stack-<date>.tar.zst archive. The directory is created before
+#       dumps run, so an empty fresh dir is not evidence of a backup.
+#       Hosts without this independent backup root skip the check.
 # repo-archive-backup is covered via its timer's last-trigger time
 # only: its script and restic credentials live outside this repo, so
 # no run record is required of it (stated in laptop-backups.nix too).
@@ -170,6 +175,44 @@ for s in json.load(sys.stdin):
   fi
 fi
 
+# --- (d) local pm-stack archive presence -------------------------------------
+PM_STACK_ROOT="$HOME/backups/pm-stack"
+if [ -d "$PM_STACK_ROOT" ]; then
+  newest_pm_stack_day=""
+  # nullglob: an unmatched glob must expand to nothing, not to the
+  # literal pattern (which the [ -d ] guard below would have to catch).
+  shopt -s nullglob
+  for day_dir in "$PM_STACK_ROOT"/*/; do
+    [ -d "$day_dir" ] || continue
+    day="${day_dir%/}"
+    day="${day##*/}"
+    [[ "$day" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$ ]] || continue
+    normalized_day="$(date -d "$day" +%F 2>/dev/null || true)"
+    [ "$normalized_day" = "$day" ] || continue
+
+    # The backup script creates the dated directory before its dumps;
+    # its mtime therefore detects a fresh failed run even when no file
+    # was ever written. Select by the ISO date, not mtime ordering, in
+    # case a later write touches an older day directory.
+    day_mtime="$(stat -c %Y -- "$day_dir" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+    [[ "$day_mtime" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    age=$((NOW_EPOCH - day_mtime))
+    [ "$age" -lt "$((-SKEW_TOLERANCE_SEC))" ] && continue
+    [ "$age" -gt "$MAX_AGE_SEC" ] && continue
+    if [[ -z "$newest_pm_stack_day" || "$day" > "$newest_pm_stack_day" ]]; then
+      newest_pm_stack_day="$day"
+    fi
+  done
+  shopt -u nullglob
+
+  if [ -n "$newest_pm_stack_day" ]; then
+    expected_archive="$PM_STACK_ROOT/$newest_pm_stack_day/pm-stack-$newest_pm_stack_day.tar.zst"
+    if [ ! -f "$expected_archive" ]; then
+      complain "pm-stack-backup: day $newest_pm_stack_day missing archive $expected_archive"
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
+
 if [ "$violations" -gt 0 ]; then
   echo "laptop-backups-watchdog: $violations violation(s)" >&2
   exit 1

@@ -1,8 +1,9 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 # Tests for laptop-backups-watchdog.sh (#1026): the watchdog must exit
-# 0 only when pm-dashboard-backup's run record is fresh + complete AND
-# both backup timers fired within the threshold; every violation
-# exits non-zero naming the job/timer. Drives the REAL script with a
+# 0 only when pm-dashboard-backup's run record is fresh + complete,
+# both backup timers fired within the threshold, and the newest fresh
+# local pm-stack day dir has its named archive; every violation exits
+# non-zero naming the failed check. Drives the REAL script with a
 # stub `systemctl` (per-timer LastTriggerUSec values from files) and
 # generated record files whose timestamps are relative to now.
 set -uo pipefail
@@ -24,7 +25,8 @@ fail() {
 
 BIN="$TMP_ROOT/bin"
 TRIG="$TMP_ROOT/triggers"
-mkdir -p "$BIN" "$TRIG"
+HOME_DIR="$TMP_ROOT/home"
+mkdir -p "$BIN" "$TRIG" "$HOME_DIR"
 {
   printf '#!%s\n' "$BASH"
   cat <<'STUB'
@@ -80,12 +82,12 @@ chmod +x "$BIN/rclone"
 
 RECORD="$TMP_ROOT/record.json"
 run_watchdog() {
-  LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
+  HOME="$HOME_DIR" LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
     PATH="$BIN:$PATH" bash "$SCRIPT" 26 >"$TMP_ROOT/out.log" 2>&1
   RC=$?
 }
 run_watchdog_jobs() { # $1 jobs list
-  LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
+  HOME="$HOME_DIR" LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
     PATH="$BIN:$PATH" bash "$SCRIPT" 26 "$1" >"$TMP_ROOT/out.log" 2>&1
   RC=$?
 }
@@ -169,7 +171,7 @@ expect_named_failure future-timer repo-archive-backup
 # offsite check: record date is 2026-10-28 (write_record pins it).
 R2_LISTING="$TMP_ROOT/r2-listing.txt"
 run_watchdog_offsite() {
-  LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
+  HOME="$HOME_DIR" LAPTOP_BACKUPS_RECORD="$RECORD" WATCHDOG_STUB_TRIGGERS="$TRIG" \
     WATCHDOG_STUB_R2_LISTING="$R2_LISTING" LAPTOP_BACKUPS_OFFSITE_CHECK=1 \
     PATH="$BIN:$PATH" bash "$SCRIPT" 26 >"$TMP_ROOT/out.log" 2>&1
   RC=$?
@@ -193,6 +195,46 @@ expect_named_failure offsite-absent R2
 run_watchdog
 expect_ok offsite-check-disabled
 
+# A missing pm-stack root is a supported host configuration; skip it.
+run_watchdog
+expect_ok pm-stack-root-absent
+
+# A fresh date dir with no archive is the failure shape: mkdir happened,
+# but the dump never produced its named archive.
+# Pin every derived day name to one captured epoch so a midnight
+# rollover mid-run cannot make the scenarios disagree about "today".
+TEST_EPOCH="$(date +%s)"
+TODAY="$(date -d "@$TEST_EPOCH" +%F)"
+PM_STACK_ROOT="$HOME_DIR/backups/pm-stack"
+YESTERDAY="$(date -d "@$((TEST_EPOCH - 86400))" +%F)"
+mkdir -p "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$YESTERDAY"
+touch "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$YESTERDAY/pm-stack-$YESTERDAY.tar.zst"
+mkdir -p "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$TODAY"
+run_watchdog
+expect_named_failure pm-stack-empty-day pm-stack-backup
+if grep -q "$TODAY" "$TMP_ROOT/out.log"; then
+  echo "ok: pm-stack-empty-day: output names date $TODAY"
+else fail "pm-stack-empty-day: output does not name date $TODAY: $(cat "$TMP_ROOT/out.log")"; fi
+if grep -q "pm-stack-$TODAY.tar.zst" "$TMP_ROOT/out.log"; then
+  echo "ok: pm-stack-empty-day: output names missing archive"
+else fail "pm-stack-empty-day: output does not name pm-stack-$TODAY.tar.zst: $(cat "$TMP_ROOT/out.log")"; fi
+
+# The same fresh day is healthy once its expected archive is present.
+touch "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$TODAY/pm-stack-$TODAY.tar.zst"
+run_watchdog
+expect_ok pm-stack-archive-present
+
+# Old empty day dirs do not create a stale-day false alarm.
+rm -f "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$TODAY/pm-stack-$TODAY.tar.zst"
+rmdir "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$TODAY"
+rm -f "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$YESTERDAY/pm-stack-$YESTERDAY.tar.zst"
+rmdir "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$YESTERDAY"
+STALE_DAY="$(date -d "@$((TEST_EPOCH - 172800))" +%F)"
+mkdir -p "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$STALE_DAY"
+touch -d "@$((TEST_EPOCH - 172800))" "$PM_STACK_ROOT/$STALE_DAY"
+run_watchdog
+expect_ok pm-stack-stale-day
+
 if ((failures > 0)); then
   echo "laptop-backups-watchdog tests: $failures failure(s)" >&2
   exit 1
